claims.concise_claim: The provisional loader prefers the documented FDD firmware interface; direct controller work is deferred unless that candidate fails.
claims.downstream_validation: M07 must identify the call entry; M08 must validate reads and error handling.
claims.notes: This does not claim that the firmware entry ABI is complete.

claims.concise_claim: M07 may use a trace-only observation gate while the complete console is deferred to M09.
claims.downstream_validation: M07 defines the trace event; M09 implements visible console output.
claims.notes: Trace-only is not console support.

claims.concise_claim: The M05 candidate uses one reserved sector, two FATs, two sectors per FAT, 192 root entries, and one sector per cluster.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 recomputes and serializes the layout without a bootability claim.
claims.notes: The FAT layout is a host-image design, not a firmware BPB fact.

claims.concise_claim: KERNEL.SYS is the image role name; M08 will consume a future M06 PC-88VA build, not execute the accepted NEC98 baseline.
claims.downstream_validation: M06 creates the compile-only VA payload; M08 fixes destination, entry, and handoff.
claims.notes: The identical KWC8616.SYS alias is not staged by the candidate design.

claims.concise_claim: The first M05 candidate is the documented 2HD MFM geometry with 1024-byte sectors.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 validates deterministic layout; M07 validates firmware boot acceptance.
claims.notes: Selection is provisional and does not establish bootability.

claims.concise_claim: Keyboard input is unnecessary for M05-M08 and is deferred to M11, with Japanese input and filename behavior deferred to M17.
claims.downstream_validation: M11 and M17
claims.notes: No M05-M08 operation requires interactive input.

claims.concise_claim: Full DOS timer and clock behavior is unnecessary for static image construction, compile-only work, first-instruction proof, and a bounded loader read.
claims.notes: M07 timeout instrumentation must not be confused with the DOS runtime clock.

claims.concise_claim: The selected geometry and FAT choices yield 1280 sectors, 1269 data clusters, and sufficient FAT12 table capacity.
claims.downstream_validation: M04 verifier and M05 image builder
claims.notes: All calculations use integer arithmetic.

claims.concise_claim: The available manual export describes a one-sector IPL load, candidate execution at segment 3000H offset 0, and a candidate stack near segment 3000H offset FFFEH.
claims.downstream_validation: M07 must confirm entry, load extent, and non-overlap in VAEG.
claims.notes: A missing image reference prevents treating diagram-specific acceptance details as confirmed.

claims.concise_claim: Bounded local D88 parsing completed, but no exact private value is promoted to the public contract.
claims.downstream_validation: M07/M08 remain blocked; explicit promotion would require separate user approval.
claims.notes: Container identities, sector data, names, and hashes remain private.

claims.downstream_validation: M07/M08 remain blocked; explicit promotion would require separate user approval.
claims.notes: Binary identities, addresses, strings, and disassembly remain private.

claims.concise_claim: The accepted M02 baseline records identical kernel and alias payloads of 83774 bytes with the locked SHA-256.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 capacity check and M06 payload-role replacement
claims.notes: This is NEC98 build-reference evidence and not a VA execution claim.

claims.concise_claim: The electronic index routes the BIOS chapters to separate FDD, keyboard, and text-interface documents.
claims.downstream_validation: M04 local evidence gate
claims.notes: The index is used for source routing, not as a numeric hardware table.

claims.concise_claim: The electronic distribution identifies itself as a PC-88VA technical-manual collection and records its own edition metadata.
claims.downstream_validation: M04 local evidence gate
claims.notes: No printed-page identity is required for this born-digital source.

claims.concise_claim: The FDD BIOS tables describe the 1HD/2HD MFM case as 80 cylinders with eight 1024-byte sectors per track.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 arithmetic; M07 firmware boot acceptance
claims.notes: This establishes a supported geometry, not that every such disk is bootable.

claims.concise_claim: The firmware interface numbers logical tracks as cylinder times two plus head.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 CHS/LBA arithmetic and M08 firmware calls
claims.notes: The two-head ordering is explicit in the text interface.

claims.concise_claim: The FDD BIOS document lists 1D/2D, 1DD/2DD, and 1HD/2HD media families.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 medium selection and M07 boot acceptance
claims.notes: Supported firmware media does not automatically mean bootable media.

claims.concise_claim: The read-data operation documents count, logical drive/track, starting sector, format/size, and segmented buffer inputs.
claims.downstream_validation: M07 must locate the call entry; M08 validates transfer behavior.
claims.notes: The current text pass does not establish the common service entry mechanism.

claims.concise_claim: The interface uses one-based physical sector IDs and continues with sector one on the next logical track.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 image offset formulas and M08 read loop
claims.notes: Logical LBA zero is a project convention layered over this physical ID base.

claims.concise_claim: The FDD interface exposes format/sector-size codes including 128, 256, 512, and 1024 bytes.
claims.downstream_validation: M05 geometry and M08 transfer parameter
claims.notes: The selected candidate uses the documented 1024-byte case.

claims.concise_claim: The FDD operations report success or failure through the carry flag and an AH status value, with documented error categories.
claims.downstream_validation: M08 error and retry implementation
claims.notes: No status code is guessed outside the documented table.

claims.concise_claim: The text BIOS document defines character and string output operations and their parameter fragments.
claims.downstream_validation: M07 must locate a callable entry if visible output is used; M09 owns the console.
claims.notes: A parameter description alone does not prove the earliest IPL can call it.
